title: Mitflits and Anabala
summary: Golarion's Mitflits reflavored as descendants of a stranded star-faring race (the crew of a generation ship that crashed on Kortos), reverted to simpler form over deep time; Anabala (a very early mitflit who has lived through the ages as host and uneasy ally of the knowledge demon Abraxas; a powerful caster, one of the four founders, and the builder of Gen 2) is a named NPC.
description:
Mitflits will be involved in this campaign. In official Golarion lore they're a fey flavor of goblin; for this world and this group, they're reframed as the descendants of a long-lost star-traveling race that crashed on Golarion long ago and reverted to a simpler form over the vast time since. They were meant to be involved in a previous campaign that never got finished, so this is a chance to bring them in properly. The user explicitly said not to worry yet about how or why they fit into this plot specifically — that's deliberately unresolved for now, just the intent to include them is locked.

Anabala is a specific, named, already-conceived NPC: a mitflit bound to a demon (captured as 'a Mitflit/demon hybrid'; she is the host and uneasy ally of the knowledge demon Abraxas, LEDGER #31) who has lived through the hundreds of years between the unfinished prior campaign and this one, making her a natural source of much-needed historical information the party can't get anywhere else. She's a powerful magic user.

The user has also already created two Mitflit variants: 'wild' and 'ascended' ('ascended' is now called High, LEDGER #31 item 19). What distinguishes them narratively has since been settled; see resolvedSubQuestions.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump following the 1950s-tone planning session. Connected to the campaign's ancestry-reveal mechanic in a follow-up Q&A the same day.
openSubQuestions: The specific mechanism: what actually happened in the unfinished prior campaign involving Anabala/the Mitflits that now explains why non-human PCs present as outwardly human — direction is locked (see data/campaign/open-questions.json #ancestry-reveal-justification, resolved), the concrete details aren't worked out yet.

Anabala's full stat block, her role/scenes, and how/when the party actually meets her. 2026-09-24: Pippa plays her in flashbacks (LEDGER #31 item 12), and flashbacks run on PF2E rules (LEDGER #26); her old PF2e sheet survives as source material (quarantine/ideas/story/source-material/the-trouble-with-mitflits/player-characters/anabala-macthata.md). In the present day she is a free agent rather than Directorate staff (LEDGER #28), though she works with the Directorate and has her own ultimate objective (LEDGER #34; see resolution). When the party meets her in the present is still open.

What Anabala's way home is. Her ultimate objective is using mitflit technology to get a way home for her people (LEDGER #34), and what that way home actually is has not been decided. Proposal, LEDGER #34, veto freely: perhaps the search ship under Kurose, which lifts at Chapter 15 in the twenty-chapter campaign draft, or perhaps the shuttle under Kortos (data/campaign/open-questions.json#kortos-shuttle).
Whether the wild and High forms differ mechanically (a separate ancestry or heritage, or not at all). The narrative difference is settled (see resolvedSubQuestions).

Whether Pippa keeps playing Anabala in the new campaign, as one of the students (LEDGER #32 item 14; open-questions.json#anabala-as-student). Anabala must be present for Abraxas to emerge (same item), so the two are linked, and nothing in this campaign takes a character away from their player (LEDGER #31 item 14). 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #33): not a conflict. Abraxas can emerge from Anabala, and Anabala stays Pippa's to play.
resolvedSubQuestions: What distinguishes 'wild' vs 'ascended' Mitflit variants mechanically and narratively. NARRATIVE HALF ANSWERED 2026-09-13 (LEDGER #15, appearance, from artwork) and 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 19): wild mitflits are the descendants on Golarion -- quite goblinoid, but cute rather than gruesome, with bright intelligent eyes -- and the only mitflits on Golarion. High mitflits are how they looked on their home world: blue-skinned, elegant, unblemished, aloof high-fantasy elves. 'Ascended' is retired as a name; use High. The mechanical side stays open (see openSubQuestions).

resolution: REFINED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31; the full write-up is quarantine/ideas/story/bible/species/mitflits.md). TWO SHIPS: the mitflits are descended from the crew of a generation ship sent tens of thousands of years ago, which crashed in a hidden jungle valley on Kortos. Its ruin is the black obelisk the founders took for a temple, and First Impact happened there. About a thousand years later a search ship came to find it and crashed too; its hull lies under Kurose. Both were buried by eruptions and earthquakes. THE WATCHER is the generation ship's navigation and sensor system, so 'the Observer' is simply the crew's own word for part of their ship. WHY SHIPS FALL (Ingram's own 'perhaps', not a lock): perhaps Golarion's gods, jealous of their domain (open-questions.json#why-ships-fall). WILD AND HIGH: see resolvedSubQuestions. ANABALA AND ABRAXAS (GM-only, not mentioned openly for a long time): she is a very early mitflit who has lived through the ages because of the knowledge demon Abraxas. The demon ruled her for decades until Anabala made the demon subservient, since the only path to unlimited information runs through Anabala's cooperation. Now they are in an uneasy alliance: Anabala wants her people home, and Abraxas wants to learn everything and feeds on information. Abraxas may emerge during the campaign -- Ingram's liked route is the party breaking into the Directorate's deepest vaults -- and she and the Watcher are a dangerous, aligned pair. Abraxas is female (LEDGER #32 item 10; open-questions.json#abraxas-pronoun, resolved; this sentence used to say the pronoun was open). Her own file: quarantine/ideas/story/bible/characters/anabala.md. The summary called her a 'Mitflit/demon hybrid, centuries old' until 2026-09-25, when it was corrected to host and uneasy ally of Abraxas, and far older. FURTHER, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32). (a) THE TRAIT: "Mitflits have this horrible characteristic, they are both extremely helpful when given the right tasks and also fascinated by the production of technology." It is what makes them so easy to use: by William Charles Baldwin two hundred years ago and now, and arguably (a reading, not a decision) by the Directorate, whose young mitflit volunteers want to fly its machines. Write it as a virtue others exploit, never as servility. (b) BALDWIN IS ALIVE (GM-only, a secret kept until the right moment): a criminal lord who arms criminal gangs with incredible weapons, still made by essentially enslaved mitflits; the four founders are his natural enemies. How he stays alive and when he is revealed are open (open-questions.json#baldwin-longevity, open-questions.json#baldwin-reveal). Proposal, veto freely: the mitflits gathering in Kurose to go home are easy prey for his workshops. His file: quarantine/ideas/story/bible/characters/william-charles-baldwin.md. (c) ABRAXAS IS FEMALE (item 10), and ANABALA MUST BE PRESENT for her to emerge (item 14). (d) ANABALA BUILT GEN 2: the Gen 2 Frames are Anabala building mechs from actual mitflit technology, biomechanical and 'more like being inside a giant humanoid', while Gen 1 Frames are Golarion technology with no living core (item 7; quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-second-generation-frames.md). (e) PIPPA MAY KEEP PLAYING ANABALA in the new campaign, as one of the students (item 14). Open (open-questions.json#anabala-as-student). FURTHER, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #34; Ingram, Casebook D13 and N25). (a) GEN 2'S SOURCE, CORRECTED: Gen 2 is built from the generation ship's technology: the original ship, the First Impact crash site at Kortos, which the Directorate holds and keeps restricted from the rest of Golarion (LEDGER #20, #34). From #31 onwards the lore files said the search ship under Kurose; that was Claude's inference, and Ingram's own words put Gen 2's technology at the First Impact crash site (#20) and in 'the original ship' (#34). The search ship keeps its other jobs: its call is why the Watcher is at Kurose (#32 item 8). (b) THE GEN 2 CORE (D13): the Gen 2 core is biomechanical mitflit technology: robotic parts that are living flesh melded with technology. It is not a living mitflit. Wild mitflits are uncomfortable around Gen 2 Frames, mitflits don't instantly understand where Gen 2 comes from, and these mechs aren't usable by just anyone. Maybe a small part of Mother is in every Gen 2, the 'cerebral glue' that makes the technology work: 'maybe' is Ingram's word, and it is open (open-questions.json#mother-in-gen2). The arc-mitflit-frame-core-link Node in quarantine/ideas/story/bible/species/mitflits.md is closed from this answer, with none of its three candidates adopted. (c) ANABALA'S BARGAIN (N25): Anabala works with the Directorate, and has her own ultimate objective: using mitflit technology to get a way home for her people. Building Gen 2 for the Directorate was her price for access to the original ship's technology, which the Directorate keeps highly restricted from the rest of Golarion so it can't destabilise the world. With the gathering in Kurose, that puts both halves of her long plan on record. Proposals, veto freely: if a piece of Mother is in every Gen 2, Anabala took the pieces from the generation ship's reasoning core under the access she bargained for; the captured mitflit who weeps at a Frame's hand becomes a mitflit who is uncomfortable near a Gen 2 and can't say why; and her way home is perhaps the search ship under Kurose or perhaps the shuttle under Kortos (see openSubQuestions). Not decided.
